verdict.rationale: Unleash documents its own scoped API keys for 'other tools and automation'. Backend tokens can be limited to specific projects and a single environment, and RBAC offers custom project roles, so least-privilege credentials exist. However, the documented scoping applies to SDK/Edge backend tokens, and nothing shows scoped admin-level credentials suitable for an agent that manages flags through the Admin API or the MCP server. missing for 10: evidence of scoped Admin API/service-account tokens for agents, a documented link between the MCP server and least-privilege credentials, permission-level (read vs write) token scoping, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Backend tokens are scoped to one or more projects and a single environment.
Unleash uses API keys to facilitate communication between consuming clients such as SDKs, Unleash Edge, or other tools and automation.
When creating a backend token, you can give it access to a specific list of projects or to all current or future projects.
Enterprise users can create their own custom root roles and custom project roles.
